Linguistic features of six web registers

Source: R/data.R
web_registers.Rd

Frequencies of 16 lexico-grammatical features in 480 texts from six registers of the web, as used in multi-dimensional analysis (Biber, 1988). Its parameters are based on the web register data of Ehret and Taboada (2021a, 2021b). Three dimensions underlie the features, and one column is the sum of three others. For exploratory factor analysis and, on the dimension scores, cluster analysis.

Usage

web_registers

Format

A tibble with 480 rows and 20 columns. Except for word_length, the features are rates per 1,000 words.

text

Text ID, T001 to T480.

register

"forum discussion", "personal blog", "news report", "encyclopedia article", "research article" or "recipe".

words

Text length in words.

adverbs

Adverbs.

attributive_adjectives

Attributive adjectives (a new house).

conjuncts

Conjuncts (however, therefore).

contractions

Contractions (don't, it's).

first_person

First person pronouns.

negation

Analytic negation (not).

nominalisations

Nominalisations (situation, development).

nouns

Nouns.

past_tense

Past tense verbs.

perfect_aspect

Perfect aspect (has done).

prepositions

Prepositions.

present_tense

Present tense verbs.

private_verbs

Private verbs (think, feel, know).

pronouns

All personal pronouns: the sum of first_person, second_person and third_person.

second_person

Second person pronouns.

third_person

Third person pronouns.

word_length

Mean word length in letters.

Source

data-raw/web_registers.R

Details

True model: each text has scores on three dimensions, involved (vs informational) production, narrative and informational elaboration. They are the register mean plus normal noise with SD 0.6 (involved, elaborated) or 0.9 (narrative):

register              texts  involved  narrative  elaborated
forum discussion         90       1.3        0.0        -1.0
personal blog            90       1.1        0.5        -0.9
news report             110      -0.2        0.5         0.3
encyclopedia article     60      -1.1        0.0         0.5
research article         70      -1.0       -0.5         1.8
recipe                   60       0.0       -1.0        -1.6

Each feature has a latent score: the dimension scores times its loadings, plus normal noise with variance 1 minus the sum of its squared loadings. Loadings are 0.75 (contractions, first_person), 0.7 (second_person), 0.6 (negation), 0.55 (adverbs), 0.5 (private_verbs), -0.55 (prepositions) and -0.8 (nouns) on the involved dimension; 0.85 (past_tense), 0.55 (third_person) and 0.5 (perfect_aspect) on the narrative dimension; 0.75 (nominalisations), 0.5 (attributive_adjectives) and 0.45 (conjuncts) on informational elaboration. present_tense loads 0.7 on involved and -0.4 on narrative; word_length loads -0.45 on involved and 0.7 on elaboration. The rate per 1,000 words is base_rate * exp(spread * latent), with the base rates and spreads in data-raw/web_registers.R, and the number of occurrences in a text is Poisson with mean rate * words / 1000; the columns give occurrences per 1,000 words. word_length is 4.6 + 0.32 * latent. Text length is log-normal with a median of 900 words, limited to 400 to 4,000. Because of the log scale and the Poisson counts, a factor analysis of the rates gives smaller loadings than these; log rates come closer. Since pronouns is the sum of three other columns, the correlation matrix of all features is singular.

The base rates and spreads were chosen so that the register means approach those of the same six registers in the data of Ehret and Taboada (2021b), whose texts come from the Corpus of Online Registers of English (Egbert et al., 2015). Most simulated register means are within 25% of theirs. The largest differences are in pronouns and contractions, most of all in recipes, which in their data use more first and second person pronouns than three dimensions can reproduce. The differences between registers on the dimensions are larger than in their data, so that the registers separate more clearly.

References

Biber, D. (1988). Variation across Speech and Writing. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/CBO9780511621024

Egbert, J., Biber, D. & Davies, M. (2015). Developing a bottom-up, user-based method of web register classification. Journal of the Association for Information Science and Technology, 66(9), 1817-1831. doi:10.1002/asi.23308

Ehret, K. & Taboada, M. (2021a). Characterising online news comments: A multi-dimensional cruise through online registers. Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence, 4, 643770. doi:10.3389/frai.2021.643770

Ehret, K. & Taboada, M. (2021b). MDA-OnlineRegisters (version 1.0) [Data set and code]. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.4885180

Examples

features <- setdiff(names(web_registers), c("text", "register", "words", "pronouns"))
fa <- factanal(web_registers[, features], factors = 3, rotation = "promax")
print(fa$loadings, cutoff = 0.3)
#> 
#> Loadings:
#>                        Factor1 Factor2 Factor3
#> adverbs                 0.531                 
#> attributive_adjectives          0.339         
#> conjuncts                       0.503         
#> contractions            0.530                 
#> first_person            0.621                 
#> negation                0.451                 
#> nominalisations                 0.747         
#> nouns                  -0.618                 
#> past_tense                              0.806 
#> perfect_aspect                          0.312 
#> prepositions           -0.456                 
#> present_tense           0.626                 
#> private_verbs                                 
#> second_person           0.518                 
#> third_person                            0.333 
#> word_length            -0.452   0.583         
#> 
#>                Factor1 Factor2 Factor3
#> SS loadings      2.754   1.296   0.967
#> Proportion Var   0.172   0.081   0.060
#> Cumulative Var   0.172   0.253   0.314
aggregate(cbind(contractions, past_tense, nominalisations) ~ register,
          data = web_registers, FUN = median)
#>               register contractions past_tense nominalisations
#> 1     forum discussion         9.55      19.95            8.80
#> 2        personal blog         9.00      29.20            8.60
#> 3          news report         2.70      28.75           15.70
#> 4 encyclopedia article         1.15      22.05           17.90
#> 5     research article         1.05      18.55           42.10
#> 6               recipe         4.45      16.05            6.95
round(min(eigen(cor(web_registers[, c(features, "pronouns")]))$values), 10)
#> [1] 0
